speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I notice you have a dermatological concern; can you describe the appearance, size, and any changes in the lesions you are worried about?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the penis and digit.

I have noted your history of heavy smoking, recent immigration from a region with high risk factors, and the non-healing, crusted nature of the lesions on both your penis and finger despite prior treatments. Given the clinical presentation and risk profile, these findings are highly suspicious for cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. I will proceed with a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis.
